main.description: Search the caller's connected MCP servers in an org at once: pear calls every known search tool of each requested server in parallel, as the caller, and merges their results into one list. A server pear knows no search tool for, that the caller isn't connected to (or whose sign-in expired), that fails or that doesn't answer in time is reported in sources without failing the search. Requires service-auth. Callable by any org member.

org.description: DID of the community whose MCP servers to search.

query.description: What to search for, typically a few keywords.

servers.description: URLs of the servers to search, as configured in the org (see network.habitat.mcp.defs#server). Omitted or empty searches every connected server pear knows a search tool for.

limit.description: How many results to ask each search tool for, and the most kept from each. Defaults to 10.

items.description: Results, grouped by server in the order requested, then by search tool, each group in its tool's own ranking.

sources.description: How searching each requested server went: one entry per search tool called, or one for a server none was called on.

serverId.description: The id of the org's server the result came from.

provider.description: The search tool the result came from, e.g. github-issues.

url.description: Where to open the result, if the tool gave one.

snippet.description: Context from the result, up to 2000 characters.

serverId.description: The org's server with this URL; omitted if the caller has none.

provider.description: The search tool called; omitted when none was.

status.description: ok: the tool answered (possibly with no results). not_connected: the caller has no usable connection to this server; they never connected, or their sign-in expired. unsupported: pear knows no search tool for this server. timeout: the server didn't answer in time. error: the server or tool failed.

error.description: What went wrong, for any status but ok.

count.description: How many results the tool returned.
